jobs.description:
About the position
The research group DARWIN (Data, AI, and Robotics) at the NORCE Technology and digital systems division is looking for a senior scientist in a permanent 100% position with the main role of initiating and coordinating large national and EU research proposals for the research group and scientifically coordinating them as well as designing novel concepts and solutions for AI and robot deployments. The group has strong technological professional expertise in data science, AI, computer vision, machine learning, robotics, mechatronics, cybernetics, computer engineering, visual sensing, visualization, advanced maintenance and smart instrumentation.

The place of work and employment can be any NORCE location. Travelling is expected.
Work tasks
The main tasks of the position will be to drive new large national and EU research possibilities, initiate and coordinate scientific proposal writing and applications, carry out the scientific coordination and management of projects within AI and robotics. Additional tasks include carrying out technological research and development projects in collaboration with industrial partners and research organization in Norway and in Europe, as well as collaborative projects with other groups and divisions within NORCE.
Required skills, expertise and experience
• 
Scientific background: minimum master’s degree in mechanical electronics, computer science and/or mechatronics or a related scientific area, with extensive knowledge in robotics, AI and perception systems.

• 
Documented experience of at least 10 years in national and EU research funding programs with a track record on initiating scientific large national and EU project applications, writing scientific national and EU project proposals and coordinating national and EU projects is particularly relevant to the position.

• 
Industrial experience is an advantage

• 
Being and having a certified project management with IPMA, PMP or similar

• 
Proficiency in English. Knowledge of the Norwegian language is an advantage.

• 
Good team working skills while being proactive.

• 
Excellent communication and organizational skills.
We offer
• 
A good and professionally challenging working environment

• 
Exciting interdisciplinary projects together with national and international partners

• 
A nationwide network of researchers in NORCE

• 
Exciting, varied and flexible workday

• 
Interdisciplinary work in teams with experts in other fields

• 
Great opportunities for professional and personal development in a new and expansive competence environment

• 
A social and creative work environment where you have a large influence on your own workday

• 
Good pension and insurance schemes, good welfare schemes and competitive wages
How to apply
Please upload your application by pressing the application button. Your application should be written in English and must include the following:

• 
CV

• 
A cover letter with a description of your professional qualifications and motivation to apply for the position

Names and contact information of two references

Candidates are expected to openly offer relevant information about themselves during the recruitment process. Furthermore, one can expect background checks to be conducted on candidates in the final phase of the recruitment process. NORCE uses external actors to carry out such background checks.

NORCE is subject to the Security Act and there are strict requirements for our employees to have a security-conscious behavior. For this position, you must satisfy the security clearance requirements for SECRET/NATO SECRET.

jobs.description:
About the position 
A PhD research fellowship is available in the Oral Physiology and Cancer Research Group (OPCG) at the Institute of Oral biology, Faculty of Dentistry, the University of Oslo. One of our group’s major interests is the study of how extracellular vesicles from cancer cells affect various normal cells, both in the immediate vicinity of the tumor and at a distance, changing their phenotype to support the growing tumor mass. In the proposed project, we aim to investigate the effect of extracellular vesicles from oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) on the function of normal cells, including endothelial cells. 
 
The candidate will apply various experimental methods to assess whether the normal phenotype changes towards a tumor-supporting one upon OSCC-derived extracellular vesicle exposure. Such alterations may include increased proliferation, modifications of intracellular Ca2+ signalling pathways, shifts in the metabolic profile and more.     
More about the position
The main purpose of the fellowship is research training leading to the successful completion of a PhD degree. 

Project title: “Tumor-host interaction in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC)”

This is a 100% full-time, three-year PhD Research Fellowship position. The successful candidate is expected to produce three scientific papers and a doctoral thesis. The place of work is Oslo, Norway.
More about the fellowship
Admission to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Dentistry is a prerequisite for taking up the position. The candidate is expected to complete the project within the fellowship period. A final plan for the research training must be approved and formalised no later than three months after the start of the position.

The main supervisor will be Professor Trude Marie Haug - Institute of Oral Biology
Qualification requirements
Mandatory requirements

• Applicants must hold a Master’s degree equivalent to a Norwegian master’s degree in molecular biology, cell biology, dentistry or in another field relevant to the research project.
• The Master’s thesis must have a grade B or better in the Norwegian educational system.
• A good level of written and oral communication skills in English is required.
• English requirements for applicants from outside of EU/EEA countries and exemptions from the requirements: https://www.odont.uio.no/english/research/phd/regulations/supplementary-rules.html
• Publications in international peer-reviewed scientific journals will be advantageous but not required
Experience in the following methods will be advantageous:

• Cell culturing
• Standard molecular biological techniques and immunohistochemistry
• Analysis of -omics data
• Intracellular Ca2+ imagingPersonal skills:
• Ability to work independently and in an interdisciplinary scientific environment
• Self-motivation, creativity, genuine curiosity about the subject, work discipline, professional ethics, and ambition
• Strong practical and analytical skills
• Good social and collaboration skills
We need different perspectives in our work

• UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that aims to provide an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. We fulfil our mission most effectively when we draw on different experiences, backgrounds and perspectives.
• We will do our best to accommodate individual needs. Relevant adjustments may include adaptations to working hours, tasks, digital or physical tools, or other practical measures. Applicants with an immigrant background, a disability or gaps in their CV are encouraged to indicate this in the application portal. UiO invites at least one qualified applicant from each of these groups to interview in accordance with applicable state-sector procedures.Why should you choose us?
• A clearly defined and fully funded three-year PhD project with established core infrastructure.
• Dedicated supervision and research-training.
• An interdisciplinary and internationally connected research environment at the Faculty of Dentistry.
• A workplace with good development and career opportunities, good welfare schemes and up to 1.5 hours per week of exercise during working hours.(Good welfare schemes)
• Membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (Statens Pensjonskasse), with beneficial pension, mortgage and insurance arrangements.

How to apply
Your application must include:

• A CV summarizing education, work experience, research experience and other qualifying activities.
• Copies of diplomas, academic transcripts and certificates. Applicants should retrieve available results from Vitnemålsportalen; where this is not possible, copies must be uploaded.

All documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language. Applicants with education from outside Scandinavia should include an explanation of their university’s grading system and a Diploma Supplement where available. A recognition statement from the Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), if already obtained, may also be attached.

About the role
At Schibsted, reliable IT services are essential to helping our employees do their best work.

We are looking for an IT Service Desk Technician to join our Service Desk team in Oslo, providing high-quality technical support to employees across our organisation, primarily in Norway and Sweden.

Our Service Desk is more than a traditional first-line support function. We resolve approximately 80% of all incoming IT requests and incidents within the team, which means you will have the opportunity to work with a wide range of technical challenges, take ownership of issues and develop your troubleshooting skills.

You will work in an international environment where customer satisfaction, technical expertise and continuous improvement are key priorities. Our IT operations follow IT Service Management (ITSM) principles and ITIL practices, with a strong focus on efficient problem-solving, knowledge sharing and improving the employee IT experience.
Your responsibilities
As an IT Service Desk Technician, your main responsibilities will include:

• 
Deliver high-quality IT support: Provide professional, friendly and solution-oriented technical support to employees through phone, email and other support channels.

• 
Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues: Investigate and resolve incidents involving computers, operating systems, applications, user accounts, access and other workplace technologies.

• 
Own incidents and service requests: Register, prioritise, investigate, document and follow up on cases in our ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Halo), taking responsibility for driving issues towards resolution.

• 
Ensure a great user experience: Communicate clearly with users, provide regular updates and manage expectations throughout the support process.

• 
Drive efficient resolution and knowledge sharing: Contribute to our high resolution rate by developing technical knowledge, documenting solutions and supporting a shift-left approach.

• 
Collaborate and continuously improve: Work closely with colleagues and other IT teams to resolve complex issues and improve processes related to Incident, Problem, Change and Knowledge Management.

• 
Manage IT equipment and suppliers: Support ordering, inventory management and distribution of IT equipment and accessories, including coordination with external suppliers.
What we're looking for
We are looking for someone who enjoys solving technical challenges, takes ownership of problems and genuinely likes helping people.

You are curious about technology, comfortable investigating unfamiliar issues and motivated by finding solutions rather than simply passing problems on to someone else.

You enjoy working in an environment where priorities can change quickly and where teamwork, knowledge sharing and customer satisfaction are essential.
Skills and knowledge
To succeed in this role, we believe you have:

• 
A good understanding of computers, operating systems, software and common workplace IT technologies.

• 
The ability to troubleshoot technical issues in a structured and logical way.

Familiarity with, or an interest in learning, technologies such as Windows, macOS, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and Microsoft Entra ID.

An understanding of the importance of documenting incidents, solutions and technical information.

The ability to communicate technical information clearly to users with different levels of IT knowledge.

Professional proficiency in Norwegian or Swedish, as well as English, both written and spoken.

The following qualifications are an advantage, but not essential:

Previous experience working in an IT Service Desk, IT Support or similar technical support role.

• 
Around two years of relevant technical experience or education.

• 
Experience working with ITSM platforms such as ServiceNow or Halo.

• 
Knowledge of ITIL principles and IT Service Management processes.

• 
Relevant IT certifications or technical training.

• 
Experience with IT equipment management, inventory control or supplier coordination.

• 
Experience with AI tools and technologies, particularly using AI to improve IT support, automate tasks, enhance troubleshooting or streamline workflows.

We value practical skills, curiosity and a willingness to learn. You do not need to meet every preferred qualification to be considered for the role.
Who you are
We believe the following qualities will help you succeed:

• 
Customer oriented: You enjoy helping others, understand their needs and take pride in delivering excellent service.

• 
Problem-solving: You approach technical challenges with curiosity, persistence and a structured mindset, taking responsibility for finding solutions.

• 
Communication: You explain technical issues clearly, listen actively and keep users informed throughout the support process.

• 
Adaptable: You are comfortable handling changing priorities, learning new technologies and working in a dynamic IT environment.

• 
Collaborative: You enjoy sharing knowledge, supporting colleagues and contributing to a positive and supportive team environment.
Why join us?
You will join a Service Desk team in Oslo where technical problem-solving, collaboration and high-quality service go hand in hand.

Unlike traditional first-line support roles, our team handles and resolves the majority of incoming IT issues, giving you the opportunity to work with a broad range of technologies and technical challenges.

You will support colleagues across Norway and Sweden, work with modern workplace technologies and contribute to continuously improving how IT services are delivered.

We believe great IT support is about more than fixing technical problems. It is about taking ownership, building trust and making people's working lives easier.

jobs.employer_name: UNIVERSITETET I TROMSØ - NORGES ARKTISKE UNIVERSITET UIT CAMPUS TROMSØ
jobs.description:
Om stillingen
Ved Institutt for informatikk er det ledig en midlertidig stilling somuniversitetslektor i informatikk i et vikariat for ett år med oppstart fra 01.01.2027-31.12.2027. Stillingen er knyttet til instituttets fagmiljø i cybersikkerhet og skal i hovedsak bidra til undervisning i cybersikkerhet på bachelor- og masternivå.

Institutt for informatikk har et stimulerende og variert arbeidsmiljø med vitenskapelig, administrativt og teknisk ansatte, der mange ulike nasjonaliteter er representert. Instituttet har 32 vitenskapelig ansatte, 2 bistillinger, 11 postdoktorer og forskere, 9 teknisk- og administrativt ansatte, 3 utviklere, og omtrent 20 ph.d-studenter. Instituttets mål er å fremme forskning og undervisning i informatikk som en disiplin, å demonstrere lederskap innen våre interesseområder og å bidra til samfunnet gjennom våre utdanninger, forskning og formidling. 

Vår forskning fokuserer på grunnleggende datasystemforskning, systemprogramvare, applikasjonsprogramvare, cybersikkerhet og utvikling av systemprototyper. Vår forskning har bidrag innen arkitektur, design og implementering av distribuerte systemer, høyytelse distribuert databehandling, cyber-fysiske og IoT-systemer, mobile og trådløse systemer, operativsystemer og helseinformatikk. I de senere år har vi også hatt et økt fokus på systemer, modeller og applikasjoner for maskinlæring og kunstig intelligens. 

Instituttets cybersikkerhetsgruppe forsker på sikkerhet og personvern i distribuerte systemer, blant annet sikkerhet for IoT og ressursbegrensede enheter, tilgangskontroll, og personvernbevarende databehandling. Gruppen har ansvar for instituttets emner i cybersikkerhet på bachelor- og masternivå.

Arbeidssted er UiT i Tromsø. Du må kunne starte i stillingen innen rimelig tid etter å ha mottatt tilbud.
Arbeidsoppgaver
Stillingens hovedoppgaver er undervisning og utvikling av nytt kursmateriell i cybersikkerhet. Den som ansettes skal undervise i, utvikle og bidra til gjennomføring av emner som: 

• INF-2310 Cybersikkerhet (Computer Security), bachelornivå 
• INF-3310 Avansert cybersikkerhet (Advanced Computer Security), masternivå 
• INF-3315 Personvernbevarende beregning (Privacy Preserving Computation), masternivå 
Undervisningen omfatter forelesninger, kollokvier, laboratoriearbeid, obligatoriske oppgaver og eksamen. Emnene dekker blant annet grunnleggende kryptografi og autentisering, tilgangskontroll og informasjonsflytkontroll, sidekanalangrep, sikker programvare, og teknikker for personvernbevarende beregning. Masteremnene undervises på engelsk. 

INF-3310 og INF-3315 er masteremner som tar for seg tema der fagfeltet utvikler seg raskt, blant annet sidekanalangrep, provenansanalyse, verifikasjonsverktøy, differensielt personvern, homomorf kryptering og sikker flerpartsberegning. Undervisningen skal være forskningsbasert. Den som ansettes skal utvikle nytt kursmateriell for emnene, inkludert forelesningsmateriell, lesestoff, obligatoriske oppgaver og laboratorieoppgaver som ligger nær forskningsfronten, og knytte undervisningen til forskningen i cybersikkerhetsgruppen. Materiellet skal gjøres tilgjengelig i UiTs læringsplattform Canvas.

Kvalifikasjoner

• Evner og ønsker om å bidra aktivt i fagmiljøet og undervisningen ved instituttet.
For denne stillingen ønsker vi at du har: 

• Dokumentert forskningskompetanse innen systemsikkerhet, kryptografi eller tilgangskontroll, med vekt på praktisk implementering og eksperimentell evaluering av sikkerhetsmekanismer.

Ved UiT legges det vekt på forskningsarbeidenes kvalitet, relevans og betydning og ikke på hvor arbeidene er publisert, i henhold til prinsippene i The San Fransisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA). 
Krav til utdanningsfaglig kompetanse
Alle søkere til undervisnings- og forskerstillinger skal i søknaden dokumentere sin utdanningsfaglige kompetanse.

Du må ha opparbeidet grunnleggende kompetanse for undervisning og veiledning på universitets- og høyskolenivå. Dette medfører grunnleggende ferdigheter innen planlegging, gjennomføring, evaluering og utvikling av undervisning og veiledning. 

Se hvordan du dokumenterer utdanningsfaglig kompetanse: Om pedagogisk mappe - Result

De som ikke oppfyller kravene til utdanningsfaglig kompetanse ved ansettelsen, vil bli oppfordret til å oppfylle dem innen et år. UiT tilbyr kurs i utdanningsfaglig kompetanse til ansatte. 
Kjønnsrepresentasjon
UiT ønsker kjønnsbalanse i undervisnings- og forskerstillinger. Ved likeverdige kvalifikasjoner vil det underrepresenterte kjønn prioriteres. Menn/kvinner oppfordres til å søke stillingen. 
Arbeids- og lønnsvilkår 
Du må være villig til å engasjere deg i utviklingsarbeid innen eget fag, og for universitetet som helhet. 

Ved UiT er fordelingen av arbeidstid fleksibel og tildeles på individuelt grunnlag. Som en norm vil universitetslektorer bidra inntil 20 % av tida til FoU-arbeid og 80 % til undervisning, når tid til andre arbeidsoppgaver er trukket fra. Som norm avsettes 5 % til administrative oppgaver. 

 Universitetslektor lønnes etter statens regulativ kode 1009 med en brutto årslønn i 100 % stilling mellom kr 680000 - 730000,-. I særskilte tilfeller kan høyere lønn vurderes. Fra bruttolønn trekkes det 2 % pliktig innskudd til Statens pensjonskasse.  
Søknaden
Søknaden skal inneholde: 

• Søknadsbrev med kort beskrivelse av interesse og motivasjon for stillingen. 
• Vi ber søker redegjøre/reflektere for sin kompetanse i forhold til de krav og ønsker som fremkommer av utlysningen. 
• Utdannelse og eksamensresultater (vitnemål)
• Attester
• Kontaktinformasjon til 2-3 referanser
• CV med oversikt over utdanning, praksis og faglig arbeid 
• Kort beskrivelse av undervisningsfilosofi/dokumentasjon av utdanningsfaglig kompetanse enten i form av pedagogisk mappe eller kursbevis på gjennomført universitetspedagogisk basiskompetanse som UNIPED 100 ved UiT eller tilsvarende fra andre universitet
• Fullstendig liste over vitenskapelige arbeider 
• Beskrivelse av søkers vitenskapelige produksjon/kunstneriske produksjon og hvilke arbeider som er mest betydningsfulle i forhold til den utlyste stillingen, og derfor bør ligge sentralt i vurderingen. Videre beskrives de øvrige arbeidene kortfattet for å vise bredden i produksjonen. Beskrivelsene skal følge som vedlegg til søknaden. 
• Sentrale vitenskapelige arbeider, inntil 10. Doktorgradsavhandlingen regnes som ett arbeid
• Dokumentasjon på engelskferdigheter, kan dokumenteres ved følgende: 
• Vitnemål I norsk videregående skole (140 timer), skriftlig og muntlig
• TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language)
• IELTS (International English Testing Service)
• Fullført universitetsgrad I engelsk språk og litteratur (60 ECTS)
• har fullført ett år på videregående eller ett års universitetsstudier i Australia, Canada, Irland, New Zealand, Storbritannia eller USA og undervisningsspråket har vært engelsk
• har fullført en engelskspråklig mastergrad
Dokumenter som legges ved søknaden må være på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. Søknaden med vedlegg leveres elektronisk via www.jobbnorge.no.  
Vurdering av søkerne
Søkerne vil bli vurdert av en sakkyndig komité. Komiteens mandat er å foreta en vurdering av søkernes kvalifikasjoner på grunnlag av søknadsdokumentene og kunngjøringsteksten.  

Søkere som vurderes å være best kvalifisert vil bli innkalt til intervju. Intervjuet skal blant annet avklare personlig egnethet og motivasjon for stillingen. Det kan også bli avholdt prøveforelesning.  
Generelt
Ansettelsen skjer i henhold til regler og vilkår som til enhver tid gjelder for statsansatte, og retningslinjer ved UiT. På våre nettsider finner du mer informasjon til søkere på stillinger ved UiT.

Forespørsler om hvordan arbeidsmiljøet er tilrettelagt, helsetjeneste, muligheter for fleksitid, deltid o.l. kan rettes til kontaktperson.
 
Personopplysninger som oppgis behandles i henhold til lov om behandling av personopplysninger. Søkere kan be om ikke å bli oppført på den offentlige søkerlista, men universitetet kan likevel beslutte at navnet på søkeren skal offentliggjøres. Søkeren vil da bli varslet i forkant av offentliggjøring.

Ansettelsen blir gjennomført etter lovverk som regulerer eksport av kunnskap, teknologi og tjenester. 

Etter ansettelsen må du påregne at det kan skje endringer i arbeidsområdet.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

UiT Norges arktiske universitet er et internasjonalt ledende breddeuniversitet. Vår visjon er å være en drivkraft i nord. Det nordsamiske begrepet eallju, som betyr arbeidsiver, setter tonen for drivkraften i UiT. Sammen med studenter, ansatte og samfunnet for øvrig skal vi utnytte vår beliggenhet i Nord-Norge og Sápmi, vår faglige bredde og tverrfaglige fortrinn til å forme framtiden. 

UiT har om lag 18 000 studenter, mer enn 4000 ansatte, og er etablert på fire hovedcampuser og sju øvrige studiesteder i Nord-Norge og på Svalbard. Våre største campuser er Tromsø, Alta, Narvik og Harstad. UiT har sju fakulteter, 40 institutter og sentre, og ledende forskningsmiljøer innenfor ulike fag. Universitetet har 269 studieprogrammer og har fokus på utdanningskvalitet. 

Akademisk frihet, vitenskapelige og forskningsetiske prinsipper ligger til grunn for hele UiT sin virksomhet. Medvirkning, medbestemmelse, åpenhet og gode prosesser skal gi det beslutningsgrunnlaget vi trenger for å gjøre kloke og framsynte prioriteringer.  Våre studenter og ansatte skal ha mulighet til å utvikle sine evner og potensial. Tuftet på vitenskapelig integritet skal vi være modige, engasjerte og rause - tett på fag, folk og samtidsutviklingen.

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in predictive control and energy flexibility in smart buildings
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
We are offering a three-year PhD position within the EU-funded FLEXI-BUILD project to develop and validate human-in-the-loop predictive control for energy flexibility in smart buildings. You will investigate how forecasts, building thermal dynamics and user preferences can support load shifting and peak-demand reduction while preserving indoor environmental quality and operational reliability.

The position is based at the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (IBM) at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) in Trondheim. Your research will connect building-performance modelling, data analysis and control with the practical integration of smart services into existing building management systems. The main research question is how much flexibility can be delivered reliably under real operating conditions, while maintaining indoor environmental quality and allowing users and operators to adjust or override automated actions.

You will work with an international team of researchers and project partners in building energy systems, automation, digital interoperability, energy services, and social sciences and humanities (SSH). The Norwegian pilot at the ZEB Laboratory will support research using high-resolution monitoring data, simulation and targeted control experiments. 

As a PhD candidate, you will work towards a doctorate while gaining experience relevant to research, higher education and professional practice in the built environment.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
The FLEXI-BUILD project brings together 13 organizations and validates its solutions in four pilots in Greece, Norway, Belgium and Serbia, covering residential, office, educational and industrial buildings.

FLEXI-BUILD develops and validates a common, open and vendor-independent architecture that upgrades existing home, building and energy management systems. It connects monitoring, forecasting, optimization and demand-response services through interoperable data models and interfaces. Technical validation is combined with a societal-readiness approach addressing comfort, transparency, trust and user control. Human-in-the-loop operation allows users and operators to influence automated decisions and provide feedback.

The pilots will evaluate integration with the existing building management system, predictive and flexibility-oriented control, use of building thermal mass, and improved PV self-consumption. The PhD will make a defined research contribution to these activities by developing the interoperability framework to improve buildings’ performance, with the detailed questions and methods developed with the supervisory team within the Building Technology research group.
Duties of the position
• Complete doctoral education and carry out research of good scientific quality on smart-building control and energy flexibility within the framework described above
• Contribute to requirements and interfaces for interoperable building systems
• Develop and test control and flexibility methods at the ZEB Laboratory with project partners
• Evaluate energy performance, flexibility and indoor comfort
• Incorporate user needs and feedback while protecting data privacy
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination and contribute to project reports and activities
• Participate in the Building Technology research group
• Participate in national and international activities such as conferences, consortium meetings and workshops
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty of Engineering’s Doctoral Programme (https://www.ntnu.edu/iv/doctoral-programme), see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information
• You must have a relevant master’s degree in building engineering, energy engineering, mechanical engineering, control engineering or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master’s degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works
• You must demonstrate relevant knowledge of building energy systems, HVAC, building physics and building automation, together with a foundation in quantitative modelling, control or optimization, through coursework, a thesis or relevant work
• You must have experience in programming and quantitative data analysis using Python, MATLAB or equivalent tools
• Good oral and written presentation skills in English [level B1 or higher, see language levels]
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Experience with building-performance simulation, reduced-order modelling, model calibration or co-simulation, for example using EnergyPlus, IDA ICE, Modelica or equivalent tools
• Experience with model predictive control, optimal control, demand response or energy management for buildings or distributed energy systems
• Experience with load forecasting, machine learning, time-series analysis, flexibility quantification or uncertainty analysis
• Experience with building management systems, digital twins, sensors, commissioning, field experiments or integration through open interfaces and protocols
• Knowledge of interoperability, common data models or semantic approaches for building systems, and an interest in translating user and operational needs into technical requirements
• Interest or experience in human-in-the-loop control, thermal comfort, explainable decision support or collaboration with SSH researchers
• Knowledge of Norwegian or another Scandinavian language is an advantage for local stakeholder interactionPersonal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Work independently and organize your research through realistic goals and plans
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals
• Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity 
• Show curiosity and strong motivation for the subject
• Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions 
• Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2 % statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Engineering within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include: 

• Transcripts and diplomas for bachelor’s and master’s degrees
• CV 
• Copy of master’s thesis. If you have recently submitted your master’s thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed master’s degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• A short motivation letter explaining your interest in the position and how your background meets the required and preferred criteria, with examples from relevant coursework, your thesis or practical work (maximum 400 words and one page)
• Possibly publications etc. other relevant research work
• Possibly certificates
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.

NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Gabriele Lobaccaro, gabriele.lobaccaro@ntnu.no. If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR Consultant Martine Sulen martine.sulen@ntnu.no

jobs.description:
About the Role (Job Purpose)
Join our operations team at the Bjerkvik facility, where you will help ensure that the cooling and mechanical systems supporting our data centres operate safely and reliably. The facility operates 24/7, and you will be part of a team working continuous shifts to ensure reliable operations around the clock. 

We are building a larger operations team and will be hiring several mechanical shift technicians across different levels of experience. The role is suited both to those who are practically minded, early in their careers and looking to learn alongside experienced colleagues, and to those with broader experience from demanding mechanical environments who can work more independently with maintenance, testing and troubleshooting. No prior data centre experience is required.  
What You Will Do 
If you are early in your career, you will: 

• Assist with the maintenance of mechanical systems, including chillers, pumps and ventilation systems 
• Carry out routine rounds and inspections and report any issues or abnormalities 
• Perform basic maintenance tasks, such as replacing filters and other wear parts 
• Keep clear and accurate records of your work 
• Learn from and support colleagues with troubleshooting and testing 
• Work safely, follow our safety procedures and report hazards and incidents 
 

If you have more experience, the role will also involve: 

• Maintain and repair mechanical systems, including chillers, pumps, cooling towers, air handling units and rear door heat exchangers (RDHx) 
• Carry out preventive and corrective maintenance, including replacing bearings, seals, filters and gaskets 
• Troubleshoot cooling systems, pumps, motors and pipework, escalating the most complex issues to our technical specialists 
• Perform functional testing, system flushing and quality checks on pipework and cooling systems 
• Work with engineers and colleagues to fine-tune systems for energy efficiency 
• Collaborate with colleagues, contractors and suppliers on parts and upgrades 
• Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures, carry out risk assessments and ensure the safe handling of refrigerants and pressurised systems We think you'll bring 
If you are early in your career: 

• A practical interest in mechanical systems and the motivation to learn about operations and maintenance 
• Good English skills, as English is our working language 
 

If you have more experience: 

• A relevant mechanical background, such as a trade qualification or equivalent practical experience 
• Operational experience from industrial or process environments, pipework and piping systems, refrigeration and cooling, the maritime sector, or other mechanical environments 
• Hands-on experience with maintenance, repairs and troubleshooting 
• Good English skills, as English is our working language It would be an advantage, but is not required, if you have: 
• A relevant trade qualification or practical experience in a mechanical trade 
• Experience from industrial or process environments, refrigeration and cooling, the maritime sector, or other 24/7 operational environments 
• Data centre experience 
• Experience with refrigerants, pressurised systems or LOTO procedures 
• Knowledge of energy efficiency in mechanical systems 
• Experience working with and following up contractors 
• Knowledge of a Scandinavian language About you 
You are practically minded, enjoy hands-on work and always put HSE first. You are eager to learn, take accountability for your tasks and enjoy being part of a team where everyone contributes. 

 

For more experienced candidates, we also expect you to work independently, prioritise effectively in a demanding operational environment, and communicate clearly with colleagues and other technical disciplines. You are comfortable using digital tools for documentation, logging and reporting. 

 
What we can offer 
• Competitive salary and benefits 
• A secure, long-term position in a growing industry 
• Training and development opportunities 
• A safe, inclusive and supportive working environment 
 

If you are early in your career, you will have the opportunity to develop your skills and take on more responsibility over time. As you build your experience and demonstrate ownership, you can progress into a more independent role. 
Equal Opportunities Statement 
We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse, and equitable workplace. We believe that a variety of perspectives enriches our work environment, and we encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, experiences, and abilities.  We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds.  

If there’s anything we can do to accommodate your specific situation, please let us know.

Strategic role with high impact

Meaningful responsibility and direct influence on products and processes

A collaborative and international working environment

jobs.occupation: Associate Professor Clinical Pharmacy
jobs.description:
About the position
We invite applications for a full time permanent position as Associate Professor in Clincal Pharmacy at the Section for Pharmaceutics and Social Pharmacy, Department of Pharmacy, University of Oslo.
About the Department and what we are looking for in this position
The Department of Pharmacy at the University of Oslo is seeking a highly motivated, dynamic, and innovative researcher with strong collaborative and educational skills. The Department has a strong interdisciplinary environment that covers the key areas of the pharmaceutical field. Cutting-edge research, extensive national and international collaboration, and an integrated Master’s programme in Pharmacy position the Department as a key contributor to the development of pharmacy in Norway. We place strong emphasis on collaboration with the healthcare sector, regulatory authorities, as well as the pharmaceutical industry. The Section for Pharmaceutics and Social pharmacy is one of the three sections at the Department of Pharmacy and is comprised of strong research groups specializing in clinical pharmacy, as well as pharmacoepidemiology and pharmaceutics. The section offers an active and dynamic academic environment, ideal for ambitious researchers. The research environment (Clinical pharmacy - Department of Pharmacy) focuses on patient safety, medication use, and continuity of care, supported by methodological expertise spanning from qualitative studies to randomised trials, as well as health care innovation and strong collaboration with healthcare partners in the Oslo region.
 
The life science environment in the Oslo region is developing steadily, supported by collaboration between the pharmaceutical sector, the university hospital and hospital pharmacy, and academic institutions. Oslo Science City and the new Life Science Building are central initiatives contributing to this development. The Department of Pharmacy is relocating to the new Life Science Building in 2026 (Life Science building- UiO:Livsvitenskap). This move will provide modern facilities designed to strengthen research, teaching, and collaboration across the health and life science disciplines at the University of Oslo. 

The ideal candidate will play an important role in shaping the department’s activities in the new Life Science Building by contributing to the development of pharmaceutical sciences within a strong interdisciplinary environment. In particular, the candidate is expected to strengthen research and academic activity to contribute to the research group’s collaboration with healthcare partners and other research groups. Documented experience with interdisciplinary work and international cooperation is highly desirable.

The successful candidate should have documented independent research experience in addition to the PhD degree with publications in international peer review journals. Furthermore, the candidate should have a documented history of securing significant external funding, or at least strong funding application efforts.  
Your main tasks will be
• Teaching and supervision, mainly in social pharmacy, at all levels of the five-years study program in pharmacy, including master- and PhD. 
• Course leadership for the main course in social pharmacy at the undergraduate program.
• Initiating and conducting high quality research within the research group’s focus areas, including contributing to external funding.
• Contributing to the development of a strong and sustainable research group.
• Carrying out examination related duties and contributing to academic administration as required. More information about the position
Applicants must document academic qualifications in their field, equivalent to an Associate professor position. The successful applicant must be able to teach at all levels and to supervise Master and PhD students. The successful applicant may furthermore be required to take on other teaching duties and administrative tasks, by request from the Department or the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences. 
What skills are important in this role?
Required qualifications that must be documented in the application::

• The successful applicant must have completed a PhD preferably in clinical or social pharmacy and have a strong scientific track record within the area.
• Master’s degree in pharmacy or equivalent must be formally documented. 
• Scientific qualifications will play a major role, with main emphasis placed on research output from the last five years. 
• Documented potential for further acquisition of external funding.
• Documented knowledge of Scandinavian pharmaceutical practice and traditions.
• Pedagogical qualifications and teaching and supervision experience at all levels will be an important factor in the evaluation process and should be well documented in a teaching portfolio. The applicant should describe her/his qualifications in view of the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) framework which includes:
• Focus on student learning
• A clear development over time
• A researching approach
• A collegial attitude and practice
• The successful candidate who at the time of appointment cannot document sufficient teaching qualifications (minimum formal requirement is a 200 hours pedagogical programme) will be required to obtain such qualifications within a two-year period.
• Teaching in the pharmacy program is conducted primarily in Norwegian. Applicants are required to document proficiency in Norwegian at a minimum level of B2. The successful candidate must also demonstrate strong written and oral communication skills in Norwegian, or another Scandinavian language, in relevant assessment settings such as a trial lecture and interview.
Desired qualifications:

• Candidates should be able to establish, lead and conduct research projects, also as a collaborator. A track record in scientific and administrative management is an advantage.
• An international research network and documented experience with international collaboration.
• Ability to contribute to the development of a strong and sustainable research group.
• Experience with working within the European healthcare setting, for example pharmacy, or with interprofessional collaboration
• The person appointed will be requested to take on some administrative duties. Hence such experience will be an advantage.
• Experience with independent teaching responsibilities and with the development of study programmes.
• Experience with planning and conducting of clinical trials as well as regulatory experience in drug development. What are we looking for in you?
• Strong communication skills with students and colleagues.
• Ability to create and contribute to a well-functioning, inclusive, supporting and productive research environment
• Strong networking skills, ability to collaborate and conduct scientific leadership
• Ability to cooperate and communicate well with other members of staff
The successful candidate is expected to have an international profile in relation to the criteria outlined above. Selection for this position will be based on academic excellence and the candidate’s fit within the research group and the group’s research profile. In addition, pedagogical competence and personal suitability for contributing to a collaborative and supportive academic environment will form part of the overall assessment.
We can offer you
• Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development.
• Modern facilities in the new Life Science Building.
• Opportunities for academic leadership and career development.
• Committed colleagues in a good working environment. 
• Good welfare schemes.
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.  A workplace with good development and career opportunities.
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
• Salary in position as Associate Professor (position code 1011) in salary range NOK from 750 000 - to 950 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, two % is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund. We need different perspectives in our work
University of Oslo is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues, could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

Men are encouraged to apply. The field of clinical pharmacy currently has an uneven gender balance, with women overrepresented among permanent academic staff, and the department wishes to contribute to a better gender balance within the field.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports.

More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.

We hope you will apply for the position with us. 
How to apply
The application must include:

• Application letter
• A research position paper (1–4 pages) describing the applicant’s vision and scientific ambitions for the near future, as well as strategies for collaboration and for identifying synergies with the existing group.
• A detailed CV, including a complete list of education, positions, pedagogical experience, administrative management, project acquisition and coordination experience, and other qualifying activities.
• Copies of educational certificates, PhD diploma, transcript of records and letters of recommendation
• A complete list of publications and academic merits and awards (if not included in the CV)
• Full text of up to 10 selected scientific publications the applicant wishes to include in the evaluation
• A document discussing the importance, interrelation, and relevance of the selected papers for this position
• Educational portfolio of 3–6 pages documenting educational competence and experience, including a reflection note in which your own teaching practice and view of learning is anchored in the SoTL framework (focus on student learning, development over time, a researching approach and a collegial attitude and practice) 
• List of reference persons: 2–3 references (name, relation to candidate, e-mail and phone number)
Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
General information
As a general rule an interview will be used in the appointment process, usually supplemented with a trial teaching session. The basis for assessment will be the scientific production of the applicant, the teaching portfolio, pedagogical and educational qualifications, the applicant’s qualifications within leadership and administration, other qualifications as well as general personal suitability for the position. In ranking the competent applicants, the full range of qualifications will be considered and explicitly assessed.

Rules for appointments to associate professorships. https://www.uio.no/english/about/regulations/personnel/academic/rules-appointment-professor.htmlRules for the assessment and weighting of pedagogical competence for appointments to permanent academic posts which include teaching duties: https://www.uio.no/english/about/regulations/personnel/academic/rules-basic-pedagogical-competence.html
 
Guide for applicants for Professor and Associate professor positions - University of Oslo https://www.uio.no/english/about/regulations/personnel/academic/guide-applicants.html

According to the Norwegian Freedom and Information Act (Offentleglova), information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure.

The University of Oslo has an agreement for all employees, aiming to secure rights to research results, see: http://www.uio.no/english/for-employees/employment/work-results/

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest rated institution of research and education with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. Its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally esteemed research communities make UiO an important contributor to society. 

The Department of Pharmacy has 130 employees. We have an active research and innovation environment based on independent research in pharmaceutical topics. The Department of Pharmacy is responsible for the popular master's degree program in pharmacy and has 350 competent and committed students.
Pharmaceutical related research and education forms the base of all activities at the Department of Pharmacy. About the project
Globally, electricity demand is increasing and expected to increase in the coming years, supported by higher consumption from industrial actors, increasing electrification and integration of electric vehicles, data centers and other electrical sources. The electrical grid is getting increasingly strained due to the increased load, which needs to handle the power-intense appliances, while also needing to enable more renewable energy production into the power system. In both the EU and Norway, the ageing distribution grid is expected to have challenges in the future year due to the energy transition, needing investments and reinforcements to prevent critical situations such as voltage issues and bottlenecks in the grid. To combat these issues due to long lead time on investments and immature replacement situations, flexibility is seen as a vital part to enable more active operation of the electrical grid to prolong secure operational conditions. Ensuring local flexible resources in local distributional grids can be enabled for grid support and be integrated as part of the operational solutions without impacting their own operational situations to a large degree will be key to understanding and assessing the potential available. 

The objective of this PhD project is to develop new knowledge, models, methods, and analytical insights into how flexible resources can be utilized to provide grid support to the local distribution grid, while also participating in defined electrical markets and balancing markets. The flexible resources aim to maximize their revenues through different market options, and the consequences this will have on the local distribution grid. How upholding local conditions can be performed will be important to enable value-stacking grid services in an efficient manner. Local distributional systems operators (DSOs) might not have defined specific local markets for grid support, and how this service impacts other revenue streams and how TSO-DSO-coordination impacts operations will need to be analyzed. The project will focus on how these local conditions can be accounted for in long-term operational planning by the flexible provider, while also being accounted for during short-term operational decisions and reserve market activation sequences. Use of both active and reactive power to enable efficient grid operations will be a key aspect to approach this work.

The PhD candidate will develop and apply optimization-based models that capture the dynamics of the electricity grid and different flexible providers in the distributional grid (for instance, but not limited to batteries, EV parking lots, industrial demand, etc.). Key focus will be put into methods that can simplify grid information, to reduce the need for grid-sensitive information during operational planning and operation. Regulatory aspects and TSO-DSO coordination schemes will also need to be addressed and investigated as part of the project. 

The PhD candidate will be hosted by the Electricity Markets and Energy Systems Planning (EMESP) group in the Department of Electric Energy at NTNU. The main supervisor will be Associate Professor Kasper Emil Thorvaldsen, with co-supervision from relevant experts in power system operation and optimization, depending on the final methodological focus of the PhD project.
